function: Reconstructs fine-grained channel fingerprints (channel power maps of a massive MIMO BS) from coarse-grained maps, framed as image super-resolution with a conditional diffusion model (pp. 1, 4)
system: Massive MIMO-OFDM, BS with 8x8 UPA serving single-antenna users, 2.4 GHz, 128 m x 128 m area, 512 subcarriers; no RIS (pp. 3, 11, 12)
method: Conditional generative diffusion model (CGDM), a U-Net variant with residual and self-attention blocks, trained supervised on LR-HR pairs; one-shot layer pruning plus knowledge distillation gives LiCGDM (pp. 5-11)
data_channel: QuaDRiGa v2.6.1, 3GPP 38.901 UMa NLOS, 2.4 GHz; 6000 CF pairs (HR 128x128, LR 32x32) from random BS locations, split 5:1 for training and testing (pp. 11-12)
test_conditions: Train and test on x4 task (32x32 to 128x128), random BS locations, 5:1 split; zero-shot test on unseen x2, x8, x16 factors, no retraining (pp. 12, 14)
baselines: Learned only: SRGAN-MSE, SRGAN, C-VAE, DRRN, retrained on the same x4 data; no classical interpolation baseline; CGDM versus pruned LiCGDM (pp. 13-14)
metrics: NMSE, MSE, PSNR and SSIM of the reconstructed channel power map; training loss curves; FLOPs and parameters (pp. 12-14)
complexity: Parameters and FLOPs, Table II: CGDM 221.21 M and 54.58 G, LiCGDM 143.79 M and 31.06 G; per-layer multiplication complexity in big-O (pp. 13-14)
openness: none stated; no link to code or to the generated dataset (pp. 11-12)
q1_support: p. 11: "widely adopted QuaDRiGa1 generator (version 2.6.1)" with the 3GPP 38.901 UMa NLOS scenario; the training and test CF data are generated from it.
q2_support: p. 14: "without exposure to the" x16, x8 and x2 SR CF datasets; Table IV (p. 15) gives zero-shot results on these unseen magnification factors after training only on x4.
q3_support: p. 13: "select several state-of-the-art neural networks as benchmarks" (SRGAN-MSE, SRGAN, C-VAE, DRRN); no non-learned baseline such as interpolation is compared, only its complexity is mentioned (p. 4).
q4_support: p. 13: "parameter count of 221.21 M and FLOPs of 54.58 G" for CGDM; Table II lists FLOPs and parameters for every method.
q5_support: p. 11: "we generate 6,000 pairs of CF samples" by running QuaDRiGa simulations; the paper gives no link or DOI for code or data and uses no public dataset.
notes: Borderline function: it builds channel power maps (channel knowledge map), not instantaneous CSI; kept in area 2 as synthesis or prediction of the channel because the paper says it facilitates CSI acquisition and transceiver design (p. 1). q2 rests on zero-shot tests with unseen magnification factors, that is another sampling density of the input map in the same QuaDRiGa scenario (p. 14). q3 is 0 because all benchmarks are neural networks.
